subject: Biotechnology
title: Enzymes in Detergents
description: A short lesson to help you apply Enzymes in Detergents.

hook.text: Cold-water laundry saves energy — but stains do not dissolve in cold water. Enzymes break them down instead.

buildup.text: Proteases digest protein stains like blood, lipases break down grease, and amylases dissolve starchy food residues.

discovery.text: Novozymes' Savinase works at 20°C — enabling effective cold-water washing and reducing household energy use by 30%.

twist.text: Early laundry enzymes caused allergic reactions in factory workers — encapsulation technology solved the dust problem.

climax.text: Modern detergent enzymes are engineered for stability in bleach, hard water, and surfactants — surviving a hostile cocktail.

punchline.text: Biology cleans your clothes — detergent enzymes are biotech's most common product.

quiz.question: How did the detergent industry solve enzyme-related allergies in factory workers?
options: Encapsulation technology contained the enzyme dust that caused allergic reactions
They reduced the enzyme concentration to below allergenic levels

details.summary: Laundry and dishwasher detergents contain engineered enzymes that break down protein, fat, starch, and cellulose stains at low temperatures. Proteases, lipases, amylases, and cellulases work together to clean effectively in cold water, saving energy.
details.whyItMatters: Adding enzymes to detergents was one of biotechnology's first commercial successes. It enables effective cold-water washing that reduces household energy consumption while removing tough stains that chemicals alone cannot.
takeaways: Proteases break down protein stains like blood, egg, and grass
Cold-water washing with enzymes saves significant household energy
Engineered enzyme stability allows function in harsh detergent conditions

faq.question: How do enzymes work in cold-water detergent?
faq.answer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that break molecular bonds in stain compounds at low temperatures where chemical surfactants alone struggle. Protein engineering has created variants that remain active and stable in cold alkaline detergent solutions.

faq.question: Are enzyme detergents safe for sensitive skin?
faq.answer: Modern detergent enzymes are highly purified and rinse away completely. Extensive testing shows they do not cause skin irritation when used as directed. Early formulations caused allergic reactions in factory workers, leading to encapsulation technology that resolved the issue.
